hints: With the shortcut wire in, click bulb B and check its current. Where did the current go instead?

Current splits between paths, and most of it takes the easy way. It's like cars picking an empty road over a jammed one. A bare wire has almost no resistance, so nearly all the current skips bulb B. The loop now has less resistance, so more current flows through bulb A.
Run it with the shortcut wire in, then take it out. Compare bulb A both times.
